rationale: Builds directly on the current best recurrent-tail QK script without spending more quantized bytes or adding runtime-heavy recurrence. The best path relies on tiny zero- or near-zero-init control tensors like tail_recur_gates, q_gain, bigram_scale, and logit_gain, but they currently share the same Adam group as all other small tensors. This split gives those fast-acting controls a higher default learning rate so the recurrent tail, attention temperature, and lightweight output calibration can move earlier within the 600-second budget, while the larger scalar/residual controls keep the safer baseline behavior. The exact final int8+zlib path, validation split, print formats, and best-script evaluation reserves remain intact.
title: Fast Control LR Split On Recurrent-Tail QK Best
